clue.text: Characteristic of Mr Worldly-Wiseman to escape in confusion?

indicators.note: letters thrown into confusion are jumbled, so the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Bunyan character slips away in a muddle, as a worldly man might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is fodder: ESCAPE plus IN rearranged under 'confusion'. Mr Worldly-Wiseman is a character in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly wisdom is the trait of the character, and the word means wisdom or discernment.

clue.text: Fairies persist in variety

indicators.note: the letters appear in a varied order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fairies keep going in a music-hall show.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves and pixies are small magical spirits.

clue.text: It is bound to succeed

parts.note: not certain of success but bound to come after, as future generations follow

explanation.definitionFit: Future generations will inevitably follow those living now.

clue.text: Book form shows up no 'main movement about one

indicators.note: the reversed letters go about, around, the next piece
in a down clue, showing up means reading from bottom to top, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the main is the sea; its movement is the tide
one is I as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A publication reveals no great movement concerning someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old poetic word for the open sea. In a down clue 'shows up' reads the pair bottom to top, giving EDITON, which 'about' wraps around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular printing or format of a book is one issue of it.

clue.text: Might " The Carp " be one in an angler's book ?

definitions.text: Might " The Carp " be one in an angler's book ?

parts.words: Might " The Carp " be one in an angler's book ?
parts.note: a section heading in a fishing manual, with a pun on a fish of the carp family

explanation.walkthrough: The angler's book suggests a fishing manual whose sections might each be headed by a fish name.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbered division of a book, which in a fishing manual might be headed by a fish.

clue.text: Volcanic aid to cleanliness

parts.note: a light porous stone thrown out by volcanoes, used to scrub hard skin clean

explanation.definitionFit: This frothy volcanic rock is sold as a scrubbing stone for feet and hands.

clue.text: Beauty judge has one answer for "capitalists"

parts.note: in Greek myth Paris judged which goddess was most beautiful
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A beauty-contest judge has one reply to give to the money men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalists' wants to mean financiers; here it is people of a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of France's capital city are, punningly, residents of a capital.

clue.text: With a mug around, Laurel could show horse-sense

indicators.note: the word for a mug goes around the name

parts.note: taken as written
Stan Laurel, of the comedy pair Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A comedian holding a mug shows some common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild horse of the American plains.

clue.text: Satisfied with what is Inside

explanation.definitionFit: Stressed one way it means pleased; stressed the other it means what a container holds.

clue.text: Form of Porter's air intake device

indicators.note: a new form of the words that follow means their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A man named Porter has some kind of breathing apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like part of the definition, but it is fodder alongside PORTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mask that filters what a person breathes in is a device for taking in air.

clue.text: What birds do in trees in Gloucestershire

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A nature note about birdsong in the Cotswold trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds warble and chirp, which is to make music with the voice.

clue.text: Play for one season only ?

parts.note: a theatrical run limited to one season, but read as a Shakespeare play named after one of the four seasons

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late romance is a play whose title names a cold season of the year.

clue.text: Top bowler

definitions.meaning: a child's toy that whirls on its point
in cricket, a bowler who makes the ball turn off the pitch

explanation.definitionFit: A whirling toy and a cricketer who imparts turn on the ball both take this name.

clue.text: Meet in French bar

parts.note: en is French for in
a counter is the bar of a pub or shop

explanation.surface: Arrange a rendezvous in a French bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across or face someone is to meet them.

clue.text: Not good getting nothing before end of play

parts.note: an old word for nothing or zero

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A child misbehaves, achieving nothing before playtime ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved child is said to be not good.

clue.text: He's always present at a rural gathering

definitions.text: He's always present at a rural gathering

parts.words: He's always present at a rural gathering
parts.note: a gathering read as the bringing in of crops, not a social event

explanation.definitionFit: A farm worker or machine reaping crops is part of every gathering-in of the harvest.

clue.text: He was rated in the Rialto

definitions.text: He was rated in the Rialto

parts.words: He was rated in the Rialto
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice the moneylender complains that Antonio has often rated (berated) him on the Rialto

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Venetian moneylender says he was scolded by Antonio at the Rialto market.

clue.text: One responsible for hold-up in a Kentish garden

definitions.text: One responsible for hold-up in a Kentish garden

parts.words: One responsible for hold-up in a Kentish garden
parts.note: a robbery suggested, but the support for climbing plants in a Kent hop garden

explanation.walkthrough: Kent is the English county famous for hop gardens, where the bines climb tall supports.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall stake supports climbing hop bines, holding them up.

clue.text: Servants almost unable to open doors

indicators.note: one letter short of the full phrase

parts.note: one who lacks keys cannot open doors

explanation.surface: Servants are nearly locked out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops one K from LACK KEYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Footmen and other liveried attendants are servants.

clue.text: Costers make good guards

indicators.note: the word is reworked into a better shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: costers are costermongers, street fruit-sellers

explanation.surface: Street traders turn out to be fine bodyguards.
explanation.walkthrough: A coster (costermonger) is a London street barrow-seller.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who accompany and protect someone are guards in the verb sense of attends.

clue.text: Note high-class spirit of the Empress

parts.note: E is a musical note
U means upper-class in British usage
a genie is a spirit of Arabian tales

explanation.surface: A remark on the lofty spirit of a royal consort.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugénie de Montijo was the wife of Napoleon III and Empress of the French.

clue.text: The faster they are the less they run

definitions.text: The faster they are the less they run

parts.words: The faster they are the less they run
parts.note: speed and running suggested, but fast dyes do not bleed in the wash

explanation.definitionFit: Dyes that are fast do not run when washed.

clue.text: Diffident quality of Aunt Sally?

parts.note: an Aunt Sally is a fairground figure that people throw things at, so it is a target for shies

explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing sticks at a figure; to shy is to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity is a diffident quality; the fairground figure is literally made to be thrown at.

clue.text: The gods of the old cinema?

definitions.text: The gods of the old cinema?

parts.words: The gods of the old cinema?
parts.note: the gods are the highest gallery in a theatre; the old cinema was the pictures

explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres 'the gods' is the highest balcony; an old word for cinema is 'the pictures', so a cinema's gods would be its gallery. The real meaning is an art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A room showing paintings, read as the upper tier of a picture house.

clue.text: European — not as far north as this

definitions.text: not as far north as this
definitions.meaning: the northernmost point of the earth, the top end of its axis

explanation.definitionFit: A Polish national and the northernmost point of the globe share this name.

clue.text: Might a ring-dove be so upset by metamorphosis?

definitions.text: Might a ring-dove be so upset by metamorphosis?

parts.words: Might a ring-dove be so upset by metamorphosis?
parts.note: a ring-dove changed into a different kind of dove, while the phrase also means capsize

explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to be upset; read literally, a dove changing species becomes another dove.

clue.text: Landlord without gold

parts.note: less means without, as in 'a year less a day'
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A property owner short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lets property under a lease is a landlord.

clue.text: Quantities of 22s and feet for instance

definitions.meaning: poles (22-across) and feet are units of length

explanation.definitionFit: Amounts poured out and units of length such as feet and rods are both so called.
